question.problem:
Which of the following values of $x$ satisfy the inequality $x-3\le 11\,?$

I. $x=18$

II. $x=12$

III. $x=14$
question.worked_solution:
We substitute each value into the given inequality and check to see if the resulting statement is true or false.

- We substitute the value $x=18$ into the given inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & \le 11 \\ 18-3 & \le 11 \\ 15 & \le 11\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $x=18$ into the inequality leads to a **false** statement. 

Therefore, $x=18$ **does not satisfy** this inequality.

- We substitute the value $x=12$ into the given inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & \le 11 \\ 12-3 & \le 11 \\ 9 & \le 11\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $x=12$ into the inequality leads to a **true** statement. 

Therefore, $x=12$ **satisfies** this inequality.

- We substitute the value $x=14$ into the given inequality. We get:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & \le 11 \\ 14-3 & \le 11 \\ 11 & \le 11\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting $x=14$ into the inequality leads to a **true** statement. 

Therefore, $x=14$ **satisfies** this inequality.
